subject: Action items and test matrix: Novacorp unit economics & heatmap
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Park <ari@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + preliminary unit economics (attachments)

Arielle—thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so everyone has the same context. I attached a lightweight spreadsheet with the numbers below (novacorp_unit_econ_v1.xlsx) and a short snapshot PDF comparing Redwood vs the hyperscaler baseline (redwood_vs_hyperscaler_snapshot.pdf).

High-level recap
- Goal: run a short PoC to validate latency-sensitive, cost-conscious LLM features (chat + reranking) over next 3–4 weeks.
- Key requirements you shared: P95 latency < 220ms for 8k context, support for model fallbacks during capacity spikes, and token-level cost transparency for finance.

Where Redwood differentiates (summary)
- Cost controls: prefix & KV caching that can reduce token spend by 20–60% depending on reuse; continuous batching with dynamic batch-size limits to preserve latency SLOs.
- Deterministic unit economics: we provide per-1M token estimates across cold/warm cache and different batching windows, plus a model variant routing policy to trade off cost vs quality.
- Private + Dedicated options: reserved pools if Novacorp wants predictable peak throughput and private networking.

Preliminary unit-econ (ballpark; numbers in spreadsheet)
- Hyperscaler baseline (n1): $1,200 per 1M tokens (no cache, single-request pricing, conservative batching)
- Redwood hosted (cold cache): $780 per 1M tokens
- Redwood hosted (warm cache; 40% cache hit on reused prefixes): $470 per 1M tokens
- Redwood dedicated (reserved + autoscale buffer): $330 per 1M tokens (assumes sustained qps and a 60% cache hit on KV prefix reuse)

Suggested next tests (short & specific)
1) Throughput/latency matrix: 1k/4k/8k contexts, 50/200/500 qps sustained for 10 minutes; capture P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, and GPU utilization.
2) Cache sensitivity: run same workload with cache disabled, ~20% hit, 40% hit, 60% hit to plot unit cost vs hit-rate.
3) Batching impact: fixed payload profile with batching window 5ms/20ms/50ms to show latency vs cost tradeoffs.
4) Model routing: measure quality delta when falling back from a higher-cost model to a lower-cost variant under constrained capacity.

Ask from you
- Can you share a small representative dataset or prompts for the chat flow (anonymized) so we can pre-config the cache prefixes?
- Which tests matter most for procurement vs engineering—procurement will want cold/warm cost deltas; eng will want P95 stability.

Proposed timeline
- This week: agree test matrix and data sample.
- Next week: Redwood runs a 2-day benchmark and shares raw traces + heatmap.
- Week after: joint review, decide on Dedicated vs Hosted for PoC.

Thanks—Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer

From: Arielle Park <ari@novacorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Novacorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + preliminary unit economics (attachments)

Thanks Karthik — this is great and aligns with our expectations. A few clarifications and priorities from our side:

Priorities for procurement (short list)
- Cold vs warm delta is critical — finance wants both absolute and percent savings.
- Please include a per-1M token cost for both the hosted numbers and the dedicated reserve example using a 3-month commit.

Engineering asks
- For the throughput matrix, can you include a run with variable prompt lengths (short/medium/long) rather than fixed context sizes? We want to see how tokenization affects batching.
- For the cache sensitivity tests, we care about prefix reuse versus KV-cache (session-level) differences — include both if possible.

Test requests
1) Can you run the 8k context, 200 qps sustained test with a warm-cache scenario (we can provide a synthetic set to prime the cache).
2) Add a step that simulates a failover where the expected model is temporarily unavailable and Redwood routes to the cheaper variant; collect quality deltas (BLEU / custom metric).

Timeline/ops
- We'll share a sanitized prompt set by EOD Friday (I'll loop in a person from engineering).
- Procurement asks that you include an early, non-binding ballpark quote for a 3-month reserved capacity option so we can model the budget.

Appreciate the clarity — Arielle

--
Arielle Park
Director, Platform & AI Integrations | Novacorp
ari@novacorp.com | +1 (212) 555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: proposed test-matrix additions + pricing note

Karthik / Neha — quick internal note before we finalize the matrix with Novacorp. I created a one-page test-matrix (test-matrix.md) that adds a few heatmap-focused runs and clarifies the artifacts we'll deliver. Key suggestions: 

- Add a KV-cache vs prefix-cache split: capture both session KV hit-rate and prefix reuse (we've seen customers get very different economics depending on which pattern they use).
- Produce a 2D heatmap: x-axis = batching window (ms), y-axis = cache hit-rate. For each cell capture P95 latency and $/1M tokens. This answers the "what should I tune" question immediately.
- For the PoC quote: give procurement a three-line example: (1) Hosted - pay-as-you-go; (2) Hosted + reserved buffer (monthly commit) with discount; (3) Dedicated reserved (12-week ramp). Keep numbers as ranges.

Operational asks
- Neha, can infra stand up a quick dedicated pool for one afternoon (couple of gpus) to run the 200 qps 8k warm-cache run? If not, we'll do hosted with tagged instances.
- Karthik, I'll draft the config we'll push to them with env vars for batching window and cache policy.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Arielle — thanks for the quick response and the ask list. We're aligned. Finalized next steps and owners below so procurement and engineering have clear expectations.

Agreed next steps (owners / ETA)
- Novacorp to share sanitized prompt set for warm-cache priming — Arielle / Novacorp engineering — by EOD Fri (owner: Novacorp).
- Redwood to run 2-day benchmark: throughput matrix + cache sensitivity + batching heatmap. Deliverables: raw traces, heatmap (PNG), per-1M token CSV, and short exec summary. (owner: Marissa / infra; ETA: 2 business days after receipt of prompt set)
- Redwood to include non-binding 3-month reserved capacity quote (hosted and dedicated examples) in the exec summary (owner: Karthik; ETA: with benchmark results).
- If Novacorp wants a dedicated afternoon run on a reserved pool, Neha will confirm capacity; otherwise we'll run on hosted and tag resources (owner: Neha; ETA: 24 hours).

Docs / links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890
- PoC folder (we'll drop results here): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-Novacorp-PoC

A couple quick clarifications for procurement: the per-1M token rows in the spreadsheet include both model compute and estimated infra overhead (network, storage of KV entries). We surface cold/warm assumptions as separate columns so you can pick the scenario that maps to your usage pattern.

If there are no objections I'll kick off the benchmark as soon as we get the prompt set. Thanks—looking forward to it.

Best,
Karthik
